Subject: Re: Fwd: tidebank_502_sample.log + failing payloads — planning repro

Thanks for the repro and logs. I ran a focused test against staging and reproduced a 502 with these characteristics: 

What I saw:
- Reproducer (same payload + concurrency) triggers 502s intermittently after ~45–90s of sustained load.
- Nginx shows: upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
- Model-serving logs show an exception in the streaming formatter: "StreamFrameWriter: writeFrame() -> EOFError on flush" which lines up with Sam's "invalid streaming frame"
- Memory and CPU on the serving node are normal; appears to be related to interleaved async flush + cache eviction.

Immediate hypothesis: race between KV cache eviction (large candidate sets) and the streaming frame writer when batching consolidates partial frames. This causes the stream to drop mid-frame and nginx returns 502.

Short-term mitigations I tested and results:
- Disable continuous batching: reproducer no longer returns 502s in 3 runs. (performance cost).
- Increase stream-frame timeout (server): reduced frequency of 502 from ~30% to ~5% under same load.
- Add a defensive try/catch around frame flush: prevented EOFError in my test run.

Plan:
1) Push a small server-side defensive patch (try/catch + retry on EOFError) to staging — low-risk. Patch attached (patch-timeout-diff.txt).
2) Jasmine will push a Node SDK patch to add a client-side safe retry for 502 + slightly increased default streaming timeout.
3) Run joint test with TideBank tomorrow at 10:00 ET; we'll test with their real traffic pattern.

I'll create a short runbook after we confirm the fix.

- Marcus
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Quick update from the SDK side: I have a candidate Node patch that does two things: 
- Increases default streaming frame timeout from 2s -> 4s (configurable).
- Adds idempotent retry wrapper for 502/empty 5xx with exponential backoff (initial 200ms, 2 retries).

I've attached the patch diff (patch-timeout-diff.txt). Testing notes: 
- In our staging repro, combining the server defensive patch + the SDK patch eliminated 502s across 10 sustained runs at 160 concurrent calls.
- Performance hit is negligible for normal traffic; worst-case adds ~50–70ms on a rare retry.

Next actions:
- Marcus to push server defensive patch to staging today (safe rollback).
- I will publish a 1.2.4 SDK candidate and share npm tarball for TideBank to test in their environment.
- Schedule: joint test with TideBank Friday 10:00 ET (matches their availability).
